{{Short description|Special case of the five lemma}}
In [[mathematics]], especially [[homological algebra]] and other applications of [[abelian category]] theory, the '''short five lemma''' is a special case of the [[five lemma]].
It states that for the following [[commutative diagram]] (in any abelian [[category (mathematics)|category]], or in the [[category of groups]]), if the rows are [[exact sequence|short exact sequences]], and if ''g'' and ''h'' are [[isomorphism]]s, then ''f'' is an isomorphism as well.

: [[Image:Short_5_lemma.svg|class=skin-invert-image]]

It follows immediately from the [[five lemma]].

The essence of the [[lemma (mathematics)|lemma]] can be summarized as follows: if you have a [[homomorphism]] ''f'' from an object ''B'' to an object ''{{prime|B}}'', and this homomorphism induces an isomorphism from a subobject ''A'' of ''B'' to a subobject ''{{prime|A}}'' of ''{{prime|B}}'' and also an isomorphism from the factor object ''B''/''A'' to ''{{prime|B}}''/''{{prime|A}}'', then ''f'' itself is an isomorphism. Note however that the existence of ''f'' (such that the diagram commutes) has to be assumed from the start; two objects ''B'' and ''{{prime|B}}'' that simply have isomorphic sub- and factor objects need not themselves be isomorphic (for example, in the [[category of abelian groups]], ''B'' could be the [[cyclic group]] of [[order of a group|order]] four and ''{{prime|B}}'' the [[Klein four-group]]).
